findings.statement: CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking: pooled UC vs control log2FC is [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], with the change in the same direction in all eight cohorts. It is a local inflammation signal: paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC is [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972], while non-inflamed vs control is only [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. Caveat: CXCR2 is expressed mainly by neutrophils, so the bulk increase most likely reflects neutrophil infiltration, not a change in tissue cells; the cell-context specialist must check this. Antagonists (navarixin, reparixin, ladarixin, SX-682) exist in clinical trials for other indications.

CXCL8 (IL-8), the main ligand of CXCR1/CXCR2, is raised in all eight cohorts with pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]. The neutrophil-recruitment axis (CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCL5 with CXCR1/CXCR2) is the most coherent chemokine module in the ranking. It has no genetic support (genetics component zero), so the case rests on expression and literature.

HMGCS2 (epithelial ketogenesis) is lost in UC, pooled log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838], down in all eight cohorts. The loss is local to inflamed mucosa: in MSCCR non-inflamed vs control the change is [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649] and not significant. It is a marker of active inflammation, not a target.

JAK2 has strong genetic and drug support but only a modest expression change: pooled log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874] in all eight cohorts. Its ranking position comes from genetics and tractability, not from a large transcript change, and JAK pathway activity is regulated post-transcriptionally, so mRNA level alone does not support it as a biomarker.

S100A8 shows pooled log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.77] in all eight cohorts, in line with S100A9 and S100A12 (calprotectin family). This is largely a neutrophil and monocyte signal from infiltrating cells, so it is a biomarker of inflammatory burden rather than evidence of an epithelial change; pooled heterogeneity between cohorts is high.

DUOX2 is a strongly induced epithelial gene, pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412] in all eight cohorts. It is mostly local to inflamed mucosa but also modestly raised in non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.8129]), which suggests some disease-intrinsic epithelial activation. No drug exists and genetics is absent.

IDO1 (tryptophan catabolism, interferon-induced) is raised in all eight cohorts with pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]. It points to an interferon-gamma driven programme; inhibitors exist (epacadostat, linrodostat) but were developed in oncology, and there is no genetic support.

MMP3 is among the strongest increases, pooled log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901] in all eight cohorts, with MMP1, MMP7 and MMP10 following the same pattern (stromal tissue-remodelling module). Broad MMP inhibitors failed historically for toxicity, so these genes are better biomarkers than targets.

CHI3L1 has the highest pooled increase among the well-replicated genes with log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875] in all eight cohorts, with substantial literature support and no approved drug. It is a candidate tissue and serum marker of inflammation.

AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss, log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246], significantly down in seven of eight cohorts. Together with CLDN8, PCK1, SLC26A2 and GUCA2A/B it forms a mature colonocyte absorptive-metabolic programme that is lost in UC; these are biomarkers of epithelial state, not targets.

CD274 (PD-L1) rises with pooled log2FC [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.974] in all eight cohorts, and has both genetic and literature support. It likely reflects interferon-driven feedback in epithelium and immune cells, so it is a regulatory-brake signal; the direction of any therapeutic intervention is unclear (agonism rather than blockade).

TREM1 is raised in all eight cohorts with pooled log2FC [gene=TREM1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.861] and has a strong inflamed-vs-non-inflamed component in the ranking. It is expressed on neutrophils and monocytes, so the bulk change probably reflects infiltration; genetic support is absent and the only drug is nangibotide (phase 2, other indications).

caveats: Pooled estimates show very high between-cohort heterogeneity (I2 mostly above 0.9) because array fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq; use direction and significance across cohorts, not size.

Bulk biopsy increases in immune genes (CXCR1/2, CXCL8, S100A8/9/12, TREM1, IL1B, IL6) can arise from infiltrating neutrophils and monocytes; a composition adjustment and single-cell check by the cell-context specialist is required before calling these tissue-intrinsic changes.
Only the MSCCR cohort has a paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast; the other cohorts compare UC with healthy controls and mix disease severity.
Genetic support in the ranking (CXCR2, JAK2, FCGR2A, IL2RA, CD274) comes from Open Targets scores, which I did not independently verify; several top-ranked genes have no genetic evidence at all.
Several genes seen in the top-gene list (SAA1, SAA2, DEFB4A/B) are measured in few cohorts and have weaker pooled support.
